mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of declining consumption (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which increases corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increasing industrial production (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressure reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary environment with high interest rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high interest rates and inflation (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.2 percentage points, the combined effect signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases > 5% MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of declining housing starts and rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong payroll growth (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 is negative for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during recessionary periods (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
